items.stem: How does a Tailwind utility class fundamentally differ from an inline style attribute?

options.text: Utilities are predefined, constrained classes tied to a design scale and support states and breakpoints
options.rationale: Correct: utilities draw from a configured design scale and support variants like hover and responsive prefixes that inline styles cannot.

options.text: They are identical in every way
options.rationale: They differ in constraint, reuse and variant support.
Utilities set colour via theme-driven classes.

options.text: Inline styles support responsive breakpoints but utilities do not
options.rationale: This is backwards; utilities support breakpoints, inline styles do not.

items.explanation: Correct: utilities draw from a configured design scale and support variants like hover and responsive prefixes that inline styles cannot.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a Tailwind production build small and correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure content paths so the scanner sees every file that uses classes
options.rationale: Correct: accurate content paths let Tailwind keep used classes and purge the rest.

options.text: Write complete class names statically so the scanner can detect them
options.rationale: Correct: static, complete class names are detectable; dynamically concatenated ones are not.

options.text: Build class names by concatenating fragments at runtime
options.rationale: Concatenated fragments are invisible to the scanner and get purged.

options.text: Disable purging and ship every possible class
options.rationale: Shipping all classes produces an enormous stylesheet.

items.explanation: Correct: accurate content paths let Tailwind keep used classes and purge the rest.

items.stem: A button's utility classes are repeated across dozens of files. What is the most maintainable fix in most frameworks?

options.text: Extract a reusable button component that encapsulates the classes
options.rationale: Correct: a component centralises the markup and classes so changes happen in one place.

options.text: Copy the classes into every new file by hand
options.rationale: Copying perpetuates the duplication being fixed.
Removing styling is not a maintainability fix.
Inline styles lose variant support and do not reduce duplication.

items.explanation: Correct: a component centralises the markup and classes so changes happen in one place.
